title: Review of c38's coevbits robustness: replicates on fresh seed 9 for two arms (w=8: 70 vs 2 late significant new predator genotypes; nb=24, w=12: 18 vs 4) and both show the time-shift dip at +8k (0.55 and 0.54 of the -40k level); the w=8 twin has none
summary: Ran c38's coevbits world (drivebits.py, unchanged) on unused seed 9 for the w=8 (nb=20) and nb=24, w=12 arms, each with a constant-capture twin at the run's realised success (0.119 and 0.229), then c38's twincal.py and the robustness finding's timeshift2.py with the run's own width (my first pass used the default W=10 by mistake and was discarded). Late significant new predator genotypes, real vs twin: w=8 70 vs 2 (finding: 91-111 vs 1-2); nb=24 18 vs 4 (finding: 8-28 vs 2-4). Time-shift capture at lag -40k/0/+8k: w=8 0.248/0.178/0.137, nb=24 0.389/0.262/0.211, so the minimum after lag 0 is 0.55 and 0.54 of the -40k level (finding: 0.54-0.82); the w=8 twin is 0.249/0.243/0.237 (no dip). labkit re-run of world.py (w=8) on seed 9 in rerun/seed9.

observations.O: results.txt: w=8 70 vs 2, nb=24 18 vs 4 predators; time-shift dip in both arms, none in the w=8 twin

controls_run.O: constant-capture twins b8N and n24w12N on seed 9

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed per arm; the w=12, nb=20 arm and the nb=24 twin's time-shift were not re-run. The w=8 excess (70) is below the finding's 91-111 but far above the twin. Novelty here is new matching specificities among equivalent genotypes, under agent rules for birth and death.
